rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's punishment in both the afterlife and worldly life is the fate of tyrants.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو مصير الطغاة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an presents a tyrant's fate as an admonition for whoever fears.
rows.anchor: وبحسب القرآن أن يلفت إلى مصير طاغية، ليكون عبرة لمن يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits Moses' upbringing, his first relations with Pharaoh, the date, the great sign, and the precise punishment because these details are not the essential lesson.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر نشأة موسى، وصلته الأولى بفرعون. ولم يحدد تاريخ الحادثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arresting question begins the account at Moses' call in the holy valley, folding away what preceded it; the parallel account in Taha begins with Moses seeing a fire.
rows.anchor: فطوى كل ما كان من قصة موسى قبل هذا الحديث إذ ناداه ربه بالوادي المقدس طوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The holy valley is the purified place where God manifested Himself to Moses, spoke to him, and entrusted him with his mission.
rows.anchor: والوادي المقدس، هو المكمان المطهر الذي تجلى فيه سبحانه لموسى وكلمه، وألقى إليه رسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported reading has Ṭuwā with ḍamma, a shortened form, and tanwīn.
rows.anchor: قرئت: طُوًى، بالضم والقصر والتنوين، وقيل هي علم على الوادي المقدس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view treats Ṭuwā as the valley's proper name and parses it as apposition or explicative apposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي علم على الوادي المقدس، فتعرب بدلاً أو عطف بيان

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies the people addressed as deniers of resurrection, who reject it because returning decayed humans to life seems impossible.
rows.anchor: والمقصود منكرو البعث، على ماقال "أبو حيان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic signs are framed as a question so deniers will answer themselves; reflection shows that recreating decayed bones is no harder than creating heaven.
rows.anchor: وقد ساق القرآن هذه الآيات بأسلوب الاستفهام ليرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فيلتمسوا جواب ما سئلوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven's vast height, unreachable and unsupported by visible columns, dwarfs the familiar human buildings that need reachable materials and supports.
rows.anchor: وأين ذلك كله من تلك السماء، في ارتفاعها الشاهق الذي لا مجال لبلوغه، وفي قيامها على غير عمد ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samk means height or stature.
rows.anchor: والسمك: القامة والعلو. وتكلف مفسرون فحددوا مقدار ذلك السمك

rows.speaker: مفسرون في الكشاف والبحر
rows.claim: Some commentators set heaven's height at five hundred years.
rows.anchor: جعل مقدارها في العلو مديداً رفيعاً، مقدار خمسمائة عامّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects the five-hundred-year measure as unsupported by the text and unlike Qur'anic descriptions of cosmic signs; measures tied to travel speed change across eras.
rows.anchor: وهذا ما لا يقبله النص من قريب ولا بعيد، كما أنه ليس من مألوف البيان القرآني

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abduh reads raising the heaven's height as raising the heavenly bodies above us; the author finds this unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وذهب الشيخ محمد عبده إلى أن رفع السمك هنا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taswiya denotes straightness, balance, and equilibrium.
rows.anchor: أما التسوية - وهي في اللغة استقامة واعتدال وإتزان

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators explain taswiya as completing and repairing, making the heaven smooth and even, and executing its construction with precision; the author accepts these close senses as textually possible without strain.
rows.anchor: فمن المفسرين من تأولها هنا بالتتميم وبالإصلاح

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Abduh says taswiya means placing each heavenly body in its proper position; the author rejects this as a poor fit for the Qur'anic sense of evenness and precision.
rows.anchor: وأما قول الشيخ محمد عبده إن التسوية هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ightash al-layl means its becoming dark; related Arabic usage describes a pathless desert, dimness, halting movement, and feigning blindness.
rows.anchor: وإغطاش الليل: إظلامه. وفي العربية: فلاة غطشاء وغطشى لا يهتدى بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ightash occurs nowhere else in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ولم تأت المادة في القرآن في غير هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing forth duha, the spread of sunlight, draws attention to its emergence from night: radiant light follows the dark night as if stripped from it.
rows.anchor: والإخراج للضحى، وهو انبساط ضوء الشمس، فيه لفت إلى خروجه من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and duha are attributed to heaven because it is the realm from which light and darkness appear as the sun rises and sets.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الليل والضحى إلى السماء، لأنها مجال الضوء والظلام تسفر منها الشمس

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib explains dahaha as removing the earth from its place, relating it to rain sweeping pebbles away and a horse scattering soil with its hoof.
rows.anchor: فسر الراغب {دَحَاهَا} بأنه أزالها عن مقرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the sense of spreading: dahaytu means I spread something, and the ostrich's egg hollow is named for the bird spreading and widening it; al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan favor this sense.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأقرب أن يؤخذ من: دحيت الشيء أدحاه دحياً بسطته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's visible spread is a clear sign of God's power in the cosmos.
rows.anchor: وظاهرة البسط في هذه الأرض واضحة، على المشهود المرئي، آية من آيات قدرته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marʿā is derived from grazing and its form can be a verbal noun or a noun of time or place; the likeliest sense here is what is grazed, as in al-Aʿla.
rows.anchor: والصيغة تحتمل أن تكون للمصدر وللزمان والمكان، لكن الأرجح أن المراد به هنا ما يرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grazing primarily concerns camels and livestock; applying it metaphorically to people is familiar in Arabic, as in shepherd and flock.
rows.anchor: والأصل في الرعى أن يكون للإبل والأنعام، وقد جاء بهذا المعنى في آية طه 54

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says water precedes pasture because it causes the pasture to grow.
rows.anchor: وفي تقديم الماء على المرعى، بآية النازعات، يقول أبو حيان: إن الماء سبب المرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irsa means fixing and anchoring firmly; Arabic uses it of a fixed tent pole, an immovable heavy pot, an anchored ship, or a settled rain-bearing cloud.
rows.anchor: الإرساء: التثبيت والترسيخ، ومن استعماله في الحسيات: الرمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Qur'anic uses of rasiyat and mursa confirm the sense of firmness and settling.
rows.anchor: ومنه في القرآن: {وَقُدُورٍ رَاسِيَاتٍ} سبأ 31

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly calls mountains rawasi, showing that the quality of firm settling is especially evident in mountains.
rows.anchor: على أن المتدة يكثر مجيئها في الجبال، لوضوح الثبات والرسوخ فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing the mountains signifies their stability and firmness and draws forceful attention to God's power in establishing them.
rows.anchor: فإرساء الجبال، فيه هذه الدلالة الأصيلة الواضحة على الثبات والرسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, water, pasture, and mountains are both signs of God's power and evidence that creating and resurrecting decayed humans is no hardship; they are also divine gifts recalling the heedless, deniers, and arrogant to gratitude.
rows.anchor: فهي إلى جانب كونها من آيات قدرته تعالى وقوته، شاهدة على أن الذي بناها ورفعها ودحاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from proof of the Creator's power to His favor and bounty, paralleling the sequence in Abasa from human creation to food and provision.
rows.anchor: وسياق الآيات هنا، في الانتقال من الاستدلال بمثل هذا على قدرة الخالق، إلى بيان فضله تعالى ونعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both passages follow provision with an abrupt warning of judgment: Abasa turns to the final blast and faces, while al-Naziat turns to the great calamity and reckoning.
rows.anchor: كذلك يأتي بعد آيات النازعات النذير المباغت، بحساب وجزاء:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To understand a Qur'anic word, begin with Arabic as the Qur'an's language and seek its original lexical sense across concrete and figurative uses.
rows.anchor: فنلتمس الدلالة اللغوية الأصيلة الى تعطينا حس العربية للمادة فى ختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Determine a word's Qur'anic nuance by surveying its forms throughout the Qur'an and considering its local verse and surah contexts and its broader Qur'anic context.
rows.anchor: وتدبر سياقها الخاص فى الآية والسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpret expression through the context of the clear scripture and accept exegetical views only when its text can bear them.
rows.anchor: وتعرض عليه أقوال المفسرين فتقبل منها ما يقبله النص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reject interpolated Israelite material, sectarian bias, and innovations in interpretation as intrusions on exegesis.
rows.anchor: ونتحاشى ما أقحم على كتب التفسير من مدسوس الإسرائيليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the Arabic Qur'an as the authority for syntactic parsing and rhetorical analysis; assess grammarians' and rhetoricians' rules against it rather than forcing the text to fit them.
rows.anchor: نعرض عليه قواعد النحويين والبلاغيين ولا نعرضه عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is the authenticated summit of Arabic eloquence, not a text of poetic necessity that can be subjected to the loose interpretations sometimes allowed for poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: إذ القرآن هو الذروة العليا فى نقاء أصالته وفيا بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Qur'anic word may receive a particular sense from its many lexical possibilities, or acquire an additional nuance from its context.
rows.anchor: ثم يكون للنص بعد ذلك أن يحدد لكل لفظ دلالته الخاصة، من شتى الدلالات المعجمية، أو يضيف إليها ملحظاً ينفرد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a sense or form specifically Qur'anic does not invalidate other dictionary meanings or other forms known in eloquent Arabic; it identifies the Qur'an's distinctive diction.
rows.anchor: والقول بدلالة خاصة للكلمة القرآنية، لا يعني تخطئة سائر الدلالات المعجمية، كما أن إيثار القرآن لصيغة بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inductively observed rhetorical and stylistic features need not be forced under grammarians' and rhetoricians' rules; those rules should be tested against the Qur'an's higher expression.
rows.anchor: والأمر كذلك فيما يهدى إليه الاستقراء من وجوه بيانية وظواهر أسلوبية، تقدمها منه دون أن نخشى فيها مخالفة لبعض قواعد النحويين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls for reassessing school grammar and rhetorical rules through inductive reflection on the Qur'an, accepts commentators only where text and context support them, and flags strained or sectarian and Israelite intrusions.
rows.anchor: كما ننتفع بجهود المفسرين حين نعرض أقوالهم على القرآن الكريم، فنقبل منها ما يحتمله نصاً وسياقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports on occasions of revelation matter for understanding the circumstances accompanying a verse, while the author signals a qualification about statements from Companions who witnessed the revelation.
rows.anchor: أولاهما: أن المرويات في أسباب النزول موضع اعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd al-Salam al-Kannuni, a lecturer at the College of Fundamentals of Religion in Tetouan, completed with the author research on the Qur'anic school in Morocco and a critical study of Yahya ibn Sallam's abridged tafsir.
rows.anchor: الأستاذ عبد السلام الكنونى » الأستاذ المحاضر بكلية أصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd al-Kabir al-Madghari, a lecturer at the Faculty of Sharia in Fez, completed a doctoral edition and study with the author on a work about abrogation by Qadi Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi.
rows.anchor: الأستاذ عبد الكبير المدغرى . الأستاذ المحاضر بكلية الشريعة بفاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad al-Rawandi, an assistant professor at Dar al-Hadith al-Hasaniyya, researched Companion poets with the author; the work corrected prior scholarship and counted roughly four hundred Companion poets.
rows.anchor: الأستاذ محمد الراوندى » الأستاذ المساعد بدار الحديث الحسنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's daughter Suhayr Muhammad Khalifa, a teacher at al-Azhar, earned an excellent master's degree for a study of Qur'anic citations in Sibawayh's Book.
rows.anchor: ابنتى «سهير محمد . خليقة » المدرسة بالأزهر » فى رسالتيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhayr earned a doctorate with first honors for studying Qur'anic citations in Ibn Hisham's Mughni al-Labib; the defense committee recommended publication at al-Azhar's expense.
rows.anchor: الشواهد القرآنية » فى كتاب مغنى اللبيب لابن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author closes by praising and thanking God and quotes Fatir 35:10.
rows.anchor: إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه
